evidence: compact clean positive PSF in the difference, no dipole; NO Gaia DR3 source within 3 arcsec and no VSX/ATLAS-VS/Gaia-var match at all; PS1 point source at 0.11 arcsec with magnr=21.88, so quiescence is below Gaia's limit; episodic detections at 17.7-19.6 in clusters separated by months-to-years, returning to non-detection between them. Textbook uncatalogued dwarf nova.

ATLAS-VS counterpart at 0.39 arcsec. G=12.70. M1's single best candidate is a red LPV.
Mira trap: J-K=1.26, BP-RP=2.64, hundred-day timescales; 226 alerts, persistent, no floor (R2b also fires); ATLAS-VS at 0.44 arcsec.

difference stamp shows a large positive lobe with an adjacent deep negative lobe just below-left of the position -- a classic astrometric/PSF subtraction dipole on a bright star; a second dipole bottom-right. Independently also a red variable (VSX type VAR at 4.24 arcsec, BP-RP=4.32, J-K=1.67).
535 alerts, dense, repeated ~1.5 mag cycles on a several-hundred-day period over seven years, never returning to a quiescent floor; ATLAS-VS at 0.32 arcsec.

the position sits on the edge of a saturated-star mask; the difference stamp is a field of strong bipolar residuals with the saturation block in the middle. The light curve also shows a single-epoch vertical stripe of alerts at MJD 60500 spanning 1.3 mag, a second artifact signature.

positive source at the position with a deep adjacent negative lobe immediately below -- bipolar residual off the bright neighbour 2 arcsec away. Underlying star is a nearby M dwarf (Gaia Plx=5.96 mas, BP-RP=3.03); only 4 alerts.

compact clean positive PSF, no dipole; no VSX/ATLAS-VS/Gaia-var match; single monotonic ~2 mag rise over ~400 d from 20.5 to 18.5 then a plateau -- a genuine excursion from a definable baseline, not repeated. positive core with a negative lobe immediately left; more dipoles bottom-right. ATLAS-VS class IRR at 0.67 arcsec; persistent light curve with no floor.

strong positive lobe with a deep negative lobe below-left at the position, and a large negative blob at the top of the stamp. Light curve also brightens monotonically from 18 to 16 over six years -- a slow variable, not an event.
